weeks.title: Thinking Like an Economist: Scarcity, Choice and Trade
weeks.summary: Is week aap seekhoge ki economics scarcity aur choice ka subject kyun hai, opportunity cost aur marginal thinking se decisions kaise lete hain, aur trade aur markets sabko better off kaise kar sakte hain.
concepts: **Scarcity**: humari wants unlimited hain par resources (time, paisa, zameen, labour, machines) limited hain. Isliye har individual, firm aur government ko choose karna padta hai. **Economics** yahi study karti hai ki society apne scarce resources ko kaise manage karti hai.

**Trade-off aur opportunity cost**: kuch paane ke liye kuch chhodna padta hai. Kisi choice ki **opportunity cost** = wo sabse achha alternative jo aapne chhoda. Isme sirf paisa nahi, chhoda hua time aur kamaai bhi count hoti hai, par jo kharcha aap waise bhi karte (jaise khana) wo count nahi hota.

**Marginal thinking**: rational log 'sab ya kuch nahi' nahi sochte, balki 'ek aur unit' ke hisaab se sochte hain. Action tabhi lo jab **marginal benefit ≥ marginal cost**. Jo paisa pehle hi kharch ho chuka aur wapas nahi aayega (**sunk cost**), wo aage ke decision mein matter nahi karta.

**Incentives**: log costs aur benefits badalne par apna behaviour badalte hain. Jaise petrol mehenga hone par log CNG gaadi, metro ya carpool ki taraf jaate hain. Policies banate waqt unintended incentives ka dhyaan rakhna padta hai.

**Trade sabko better off kar sakta hai**: jab log ya desh us kaam mein specialise karte hain jisme woh relatively achhe hain aur phir exchange karte hain, to total output badhta hai. Trade zero-sum game nahi hai.

**Markets aur invisible hand**: market economy mein lakhon buyers aur sellers apne fayde ke liye decide karte hain, aur **prices** signal ka kaam karte hain. Adam Smith ne ise 'invisible hand' kaha. Par **market failure** (jaise pollution, monopoly) mein government intervention outcome sudhaar sakta hai.

**Production Possibilities Frontier (PPF)**: do goods ke wo combinations jo economy apne saare resources aur technology se maximum bana sakti hai. PPF ke andar ka point = inefficient (resources idle), bahar ka point = abhi possible nahi. Bowed-out PPF ka matlab hai **increasing opportunity cost**, kyunki har resource har kaam mein utna achha nahi hota.

example.problem: Riya ek Sunday ko 3 ghante ki data-analytics workshop attend karna chahti hai jiski fees ₹500 hai. Agar wo workshop na jaaye to un 3 ghanton mein ₹300 per ghanta ki tuition padha sakti hai. Lunch (₹150) wo dono cases mein karegi. Workshop ki opportunity cost kya hai?
steps: Opportunity cost = jo kuch workshop ki wajah se chhodna padta hai.
Lunch ₹150 dono choices mein hota, isliye ye workshop ki wajah se nahi hai, ise count nahi karenge.
Total = ₹500 + ₹900 = **₹1,400**. Riya ko workshop tabhi jaana chahiye jab uske liye workshop ka benefit kam se kam ₹1,400 ke barabar ho.

mistakes: Opportunity cost mein sirf paise wala kharcha ginna aur chhoda hua time ya kamaai bhool jaana. Fix: hamesha poocho 'is choice ki wajah se maine kya chhoda?'
Sunk cost ko decision mein ginna, jaise 'itna paisa laga diya hai, ab project chhod nahi sakte'. Fix: sirf aage aane wale extra benefit aur extra cost compare karo.
Average cost se decision lena jab sawaal ek extra unit ka ho. Fix: ek aur unit ke liye marginal cost dekho, average nahi.
revision: Scarcity ⇒ choice ⇒ trade-off.
Opportunity cost = sabse achha chhoda hua alternative (paisa + time + kamaai).
Decision rule: marginal benefit ≥ marginal cost; sunk cost ignore karo.
Log incentives ke hisaab se behaviour badalte hain.
PPF ke andar = inefficient, bahar = unattainable, bowed-out = increasing opportunity cost.

questions.question: Economics mein **scarcity** ka sabse sahi matlab kya hai?
options: Kisi cheez ka market mein bilkul na milna
Sirf garib deshon mein resources ki kami
Wants unlimited hain par resources limited, isliye choice karni padti hai
Prices ka bahut zyada ho jaana
questions.explanation: Scarcity ka matlab hai ki resources humari saari wants poori karne ke liye kaafi nahi hain, isliye choose karna padta hai. Ye ameer deshon aur ameer logon par bhi laagu hota hai (unka time bhi limited hai). Option A trap hai: koi cheez market mein mil rahi ho tab bhi wo scarce hai, kyunki use paane ke liye kuch chhodna padta hai.

questions.question: Rahul ek saal ka full-time MBA karne ka sochta hai. Iski opportunity cost mein kya shamil hai?
options: Fees aur wo salary jo wo us saal job karke kamaata
Fees aur wo khana jo wo waise bhi khaata
Sirf wo salary jo wo job karke kamaata
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost mein wo sab aata hai jo MBA ki wajah se chhodna pada: fees (seedha kharcha) aur chhodi hui salary. Khana to wo MBA kare ya na kare, khaayega, isliye wo MBA ki cost nahi hai. Sirf fees ginna sabse common galti hai, kyunki forgone salary aksar MBA ki sabse badi cost hoti hai.

questions.question: Neha ko IPL match ka free ticket mila hai (ise bech nahi sakti). Usi shaam wo 4 ghante ₹250 per ghanta ki tuition padha sakti thi. Stadium aane-jaane ka kharcha ₹150 hai. Match dekhne ki opportunity cost kitni hai?
questions.explanation: Chhodi hui kamaai = 4 × ₹250 = ₹1,000, aur travel = ₹150. Total opportunity cost = ₹1,150. '₹0' wala option sabse bada trap hai: ticket free hone se match free nahi ho jaata, kyunki time ki bhi value hai. ₹150 tab aata hai jab sirf jeb se jaane wala paisa gino.

questions.question: Ek startup ek app par ₹50 lakh kharch kar chuka hai (ye paisa wapas nahi milega). App poori hone par ₹15 lakh revenue expected hai, aur adhoori app se kuch nahi milega. App poori karne ke liye startup ko maximum kitna aur kharch karna chahiye taaki decision fayde ka rahe?
options: ₹0, project band karo kyunki ₹15 lakh se ₹50 lakh recover nahi hoga
₹50 lakh tak, taaki pehle ka kharcha justify ho
questions.explanation: ₹50 lakh sunk cost hai, wo har haal mein ja chuka hai. Aage ka decision sirf marginal benefit (₹15 lakh) aur marginal cost (bacha hua kharcha) par depend karta hai. Jab tak bacha hua kharcha ₹15 lakh se kam hai, app poori karna better hai. Option A sunk cost ko decision mein ginne ki galti hai.

questions.question: Ek economy ke PPF ke kuch points neeche diye hain. Rice ko 40 se 60 tonnes karne par, rice ki har extra tonne ki opportunity cost kitni hai?
questions.explanation: Rice 40 se 60 karne par cloth 70 se 40 hota hai, yaani 30 units cloth chhoda 20 tonnes rice ke liye. Per tonne = 30 / 20 = 1.5 units cloth. 30 total cost hai, per tonne nahi, aur 0.67 ratio ulta lene (20 / 30) se aata hai. Pehle steps mein cost 0.5 aur 1 thi, ab 1.5 hai: ye increasing opportunity cost hai.

questions.question: Ek bus company ki 40-seat bus ka ek trip ka total cost ₹20,000 hai, yaani ₹500 per seat average. Bus nikalne wali hai aur 5 seats khaali hain. Ek extra passenger ko le jaane ka extra cost (thoda fuel, paani ki bottle) sirf ₹30 hai. Kis price se upar ek khaali seat bechna company ke liye fayde ka hai?
questions.explanation: Trip to waise bhi jaayegi, isliye ₹20,000 ka decision par koi asar nahi. Ek extra passenger ka marginal cost ₹30 hai, to ₹30 se zyada jo bhi mile wo profit badhata hai. ₹500 average cost hai, aur average cost se decision lena yahan galat hai: ₹200 wala passenger mana karne se company ₹170 kho deti.

questions.question: Aman ne ek concert ka non-refundable ticket ₹2,000 mein kharida. Concert ke din use tez bukhaar hai. Jaane ka decision lete waqt ₹2,000 ko kaise treat karna chahiye?
options: Ignore karna chahiye, kyunki ye sunk cost hai aur wapas nahi aayega
Concert zaroor jaana chahiye taaki ₹2,000 waste na ho
₹2,000 ko concert jaane ke benefit mein jod dena chahiye
₹2,000 ko na jaane ki opportunity cost mein ginna chahiye
questions.explanation: ₹2,000 dono cases mein wapas nahi milega, chahe Aman jaaye ya na jaaye, isliye ye **sunk cost** hai aur decision mein matter nahi karta. Use sirf aage ka benefit (concert ka maza) aur aage ka cost (bukhaar mein jaane ki takleef) compare karna chahiye. 'Paisa waste na ho' wali soch sunk cost trap hai, aur benefit ya opportunity cost mein wahi aata hai jo is choice ki wajah se badalta hai.

questions.question: Ek shehar mein metro ka monthly pass sasta kar diya gaya aur office areas mein parking charges badha diye gaye. Economics ke principles ke hisaab se sabse zyada kya hone ki ummeed hai?
options: Log apni travel habits bilkul nahi badlenge
Kuch log car chhod kar metro use karne lagenge
Car use badhega, kyunki mehngi parking premium lagegi
Sirf metro ki revenue badhegi, travel pattern same rahega
questions.explanation: Log **incentives** par react karte hain. Metro sasti hui aur car ka cost (parking) badha, to relative cost car ke against shift hua, aur kuch log metro ki taraf jaayenge. 'Habits nahi badlengi' maanna incentives ko ignore karta hai, mehngi parking se car use badhna ulta logic hai, aur metro ki revenue ka badlaav bhi travel pattern badalne se hi aata hai.

questions.question: Ek economy ke **PPF** ke andar (curve se neeche) wala point kya dikhaata hai?
options: Ek combination jo abhi ke resources se possible hi nahi
Resources idle hain ya inefficiently use ho rahe hain
Economy ne nayi technology adopt kar li hai
questions.explanation: PPF ke andar ka point possible hai par **inefficient** hai: kuch resources (jaise unemployed workers ya band machines) idle hain, isliye dono goods zyada ban sakte the. Maximum production PPF ke upar ke points hain, abhi impossible combinations PPF ke bahar hote hain, aur nayi technology poore PPF ko bahar shift karti hai, andar ka point nahi banati.

questions.question: Karan ek weekend ka 2 din ka coding bootcamp join karta hai jiski fees ₹3,000 hai. Bootcamp ki wajah se wo dono din ki freelance kamaai ₹1,500 per din chhodta hai aur ₹400 extra travel par kharch karta hai. Bootcamp mein wo ₹200 ka khana khaata hai, jo ghar par bhi utna hi khaata. Bootcamp ki opportunity cost kitni hai?
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost = fees ₹3,000 + chhodi hui kamaai 2 × ₹1,500 = ₹3,000 + extra travel ₹400 = **₹6,400**. Khana ₹200 dono cases mein hota, isliye nahi ginenge; use jodne se ₹6,600 aata hai. ₹3,400 sirf cash kharcha (fees + travel) hai jo chhodi kamaai bhool jaata hai, aur ₹6,000 mein travel ka extra kharcha chhoot gaya.

questions.question: Ek ice-cream unit roz 500 cones banaati hai aur uska average cost ₹20 per cone hai. Ek hotel 100 extra cones ₹15 per cone mein khareedna chahta hai. Unit ke paas spare capacity hai, aur in 100 extra cones ka extra cost (milk, sugar, cone) ₹12 per cone hai. Unit ko kya karna chahiye?
options: Order lena chahiye, kyunki ₹15 extra cost ₹12 se zyada hai
Order mana karna chahiye, kyunki ₹15 average cost ₹20 se kam hai
Order sirf ₹20 ya usse zyada price par lena chahiye
Order lene ya na lene se profit par koi farq nahi padega
questions.explanation: Sawaal ek extra order ka hai, isliye **marginal** cost dekho: har extra cone ₹15 − ₹12 = ₹3 profit deta hai, yaani 100 cones par ₹300 zyada profit. ₹20 average cost mein fixed costs bhi hain jo order lo ya na lo waise hi lagenge, isliye average se compare karna trap hai. ₹20 ki minimum price bhi isi galti se aati hai, aur ₹300 ka extra profit dikhaata hai ki farq padta hai.

questions.question: Ek economy ka PPF in points se banta hai (wheat tonnes, cars): (0, 100), (20, 90), (40, 75), (60, 50), (80, 0). Economy abhi (20, 90) par hai aur 60 tonnes wheat chahti hai. Kitni cars chhodni padengi, aur last 20 tonnes wheat ki per-tonne opportunity cost kitni hai?
questions.explanation: Wheat 20 se 60 karne par cars 90 se 50 ho jaati hain, yaani 40 cars chhodni padti hain. Last 20 tonnes (40 se 60) mein cars 75 se 50 hoti hain: 25 ÷ 20 = **1.25 cars per tonne**. '1 car per tonne' poori range ka average hai (40 ÷ 40), last tonnes ka cost nahi. 50 cars mein starting point (0, 100) le liya gaya, aur 0.75 pichle step (20 se 40: 15 ÷ 20) ki cost hai. Cost badh rahi hai kyunki PPF bowed-out hai.

questions.question: Ek student decide kar raha hai ki exam se pehle kitne extra ghante padhe. Har extra ghante ka marginal benefit (better marks ki value) kramashah ₹500, ₹400, ₹300, ₹200 aur ₹100 hai. Har ghante ka marginal cost (chhodi hui tuition kamaai) ₹250 hai. Use kitne ghante padhna chahiye?
questions.explanation: Marginal rule: ek aur ghanta tabhi padho jab us ghante ka MB ≥ MC (₹250). Pehle teen ghante (₹500, ₹400, ₹300) ye test pass karte hain, chautha (₹200) nahi, isliye **3 ghante**. 5 ghante total benefit (₹1,500) aur total cost (₹1,250) compare karne se aata hai, jo 4th aur 5th ghante ke loss ko chhupa deta hai. 4 ghante average benefit (₹1,400 ÷ 4 = ₹350) ko MC se compare karne se aata hai, aur 2 ghante mein teesra faydemand ghanta chhoot jaata hai.

questions.question: Ek office mein Asha 1 ghante mein 4 reports ya 8 slides bana sakti hai, aur Bhanu 1 ghante mein 1 report ya 4 slides. Kaam baantne ke baare mein kya sahi hai?
options: Asha reports aur Bhanu slides banaye; dono ka fayda ho sakta hai
Asha dono mein tez hai, isliye kaam baantne se koi fayda nahi
Asha slides aur Bhanu reports banaye, kyunki Asha slides mein 2 guna tez hai
Bhanu kuch na banaye aur saara kaam Asha kare
questions.explanation: Asha ke liye 1 report ki opportunity cost = 8 ÷ 4 = 2 slides, Bhanu ke liye = 4 ÷ 1 = 4 slides. Report Asha ke liye sasti hai, aur slide Bhanu ke liye (0.25 report vs Asha ki 0.5 report). Isliye Asha reports aur Bhanu slides mein specialise karein aur kaam exchange karein. Asha dono mein tez hai (absolute advantage), par kaam ka pattern **comparative advantage** se decide hota hai, isliye 'koi fayda nahi' aur 'Asha sab kare' galat hain. Asha ko slides dena ulta hai, kyunki slides mein uski opportunity cost Bhanu se zyada hai.

questions.question: Ek company ek naye product ki research par ₹80 lakh kharch kar chuki hai (ye wapas nahi milega). Launch ke liye ₹30 lakh aur chahiye, aur launch se ₹50 lakh revenue expected hai. Doosra option: research ka patent ₹25 lakh mein bech dena (tab launch nahi hoga). Company ke liye best decision kya hai?
options: Launch karo, kyunki ₹50 lakh revenue ₹30 lakh extra cost se zyada hai
Patent becho, kyunki launch ka net ₹20 lakh patent ke ₹25 lakh se kam hai
Kuch mat karo, kyunki ₹80 lakh kabhi recover nahi hoga
Launch karo, taaki ₹80 lakh ki research waste na ho
questions.explanation: ₹80 lakh **sunk cost** hai, dono options mein wapas nahi aayega, isliye ise ignore karo. Launch: ₹50 lakh − ₹30 lakh = ₹20 lakh net. Patent bechna: ₹25 lakh. Launch ki asli opportunity cost mein chhoda hua ₹25 lakh bhi aata hai, to patent bechna ₹5 lakh better hai. 'Revenue extra cost se zyada hai' wala option ye opportunity cost bhool jaata hai, aur 'research waste na ho' ya 'recover nahi hoga' dono sunk cost ko decision mein ginne ki galti hain.

weeks.title: Demand, Supply and Market Equilibrium
weeks.summary: Is week aap demand aur supply ke laws, unke determinants, curve ke shift aur curve par movement ka farq, aur equilibrium price-quantity ko graph aur algebra dono se nikaalna seekhoge.
concepts: **Law of demand**: baaki sab same rahe (ceteris paribus) to price badhne par **quantity demanded** girti hai. Isliye demand curve neeche ki taraf slope karta hai. Market demand = saare buyers ki individual demands ka horizontal sum.

**Demand ke determinants (shifters)**: income, related goods ki prices, tastes, expectations aur buyers ki sankhya. **Normal good** ki demand income ke saath badhti hai, **inferior good** ki girti hai. **Substitutes** (chai-coffee): ek ki price badhe to doosre ki demand badhti hai. **Complements** (petrol-car): ek ki price badhe to doosre ki demand girti hai.

**Shift vs movement**: good ki apni price badle to curve ke upar **movement** hota hai (quantity demanded/supplied badalti hai). Koi aur determinant badle to poora **curve shift** hota hai (demand/supply badalti hai). Exam mein ye farq sabse zyada poocha jaata hai.

**Law of supply**: price badhne par sellers zyada bechna chahte hain, isliye supply curve upar ki taraf slope karta hai. Supply ke shifters: input prices, technology, expectations aur sellers ki sankhya. Input sasta ya better technology ⇒ supply right shift.

**Equilibrium**: jahan quantity demanded = quantity supplied. Price equilibrium se upar ho to **surplus** (excess supply) hota hai aur price girti hai; neeche ho to **shortage** (excess demand) hoti hai aur price badhti hai. Ise law of supply and demand kehte hain.

**Algebra se equilibrium**: agar Qd = a − bP aur Qs = c + dP, to a − bP = c + dP rakho, P* = (a − c)/(b + d) nikaalo, phir kisi bhi equation mein daal ke Q* nikaalo. Hamesha dono equations mein daal ke check karo.

**Shifts ka asar**: demand badhe ⇒ P aur Q dono badhte hain. Supply badhe ⇒ P girta hai, Q badhta hai. Dono saath shift hon to ek variable pakka pata chalta hai aur doosra shifts ke size par depend karta hai.

example.problem: Ek shehar ke onion market mein (illustrative numbers) Qd = 120 − 2P aur Qs = −30 + 3P hai, jahan P ₹ per kg hai aur Q hazaar kg per din. Equilibrium nikaalo, aur batao ki agar price ₹20 par atak jaaye to kya hoga.
steps: Qd > Qs, to 80 − 30 = 50 hazaar kg ki shortage hai. Buyers zyada pay karne ko ready honge aur price upar jaayegi.
Answer: **equilibrium P* = ₹30, Q* = 60 hazaar kg**; ₹20 par 50 hazaar kg ki shortage.

mistakes: Good ki apni price badalne ko 'demand badh gayi' kehna. Apni price se sirf quantity demanded badalti hai (movement); demand curve tab shift hota hai jab koi aur factor badle.
Shortage ko surplus samajhna. Fix: price equilibrium se neeche ⇒ Qd > Qs ⇒ shortage; upar ⇒ surplus.
Equilibrium P nikaal ke Q check na karna. Fix: P* ko dono equations mein daalo; dono se same Q aana chahiye.
revision: Apni price badle ⇒ curve par movement; baaki factor badle ⇒ curve shift.
Substitute ki price ↑ ⇒ demand ↑; complement ki price ↑ ⇒ demand ↓.
Normal good: income ↑ ⇒ demand ↑; inferior good: income ↑ ⇒ demand ↓.
P < P* ⇒ shortage, P > P* ⇒ surplus.
Qd = a − bP, Qs = c + dP ⇒ P* = (a − c)/(b + d).

questions.question: Chai ki price badh jaati hai. Coffee (jo chai ka substitute hai) ke market mein kya hoga?
options: Coffee ka demand curve left shift hoga
Coffee ka demand curve right shift hoga
Coffee ke demand curve par movement hoga
Coffee market par koi asar nahi
questions.explanation: Chai mehngi hone par kuch log coffee ki taraf shift karte hain, to har coffee price par zyada coffee demand hogi: coffee ka demand curve right shift. Movement tab hota jab coffee ki apni price badalti. Left shift complements ke case mein hota hai.

questions.question: Petrol ki price girti hai. Petrol ke market mein ise kaise describe karenge?
options: Petrol ka demand curve right shift hua
Petrol ka supply curve right shift hua
Petrol ka demand curve left shift hua
Demand curve par movement hua aur quantity demanded badhi
questions.explanation: Petrol ki apni price badli hai, isliye ye same demand curve par neeche ki taraf movement hai: quantity demanded badhti hai, demand nahi. 'Demand curve right shift' sabse common trap hai; wo tab hota jab income ya kisi related good ki price jaisa koi aur factor badalta.

questions.question: Ek market mein Qd = 200 − 4P aur Qs = 20 + 2P hai. Equilibrium price aur quantity kya hai?
questions.explanation: 200 − 4P = 20 + 2P ⇒ 180 = 6P ⇒ P = 30. Q = 200 − 120 = 80, aur check: 20 + 60 = 80 ✓. P = 36.67 tab aata hai jab 20 ko doosri side le jaate waqt sign galat ho jaaye (200 + 20 = 6P). P = 90 tab aata hai jab −4P ko doosri side le jaana bhool jao.

questions.question: Usi market mein (Qd = 200 − 4P, Qs = 20 + 2P) agar price ₹20 par fix ho jaaye, to kya hoga?
questions.explanation: P = 20 par Qd = 200 − 80 = 120 aur Qs = 20 + 40 = 60. Qd > Qs, to shortage = 120 − 60 = 60 units. Price equilibrium (₹30) se neeche hai, isliye surplus nahi ho sakta. 120 sirf quantity demanded hai, shortage nahi.

questions.question: Maan lo ek shehar mein local bus travel ek **inferior good** hai. Logon ki income badhne par bus travel ke market mein equilibrium price aur quantity ka kya hoga (supply same rahe)?
questions.explanation: Inferior good ki demand income badhne par girti hai (log cab ya apni gaadi lene lagte hain). Demand curve left shift ⇒ supply curve ke along neeche aate hain: price aur quantity dono girte hain. Option A normal good ka answer hai, wahi sabse tempting trap hai.

questions.question: Ek saal achhe mausam se aam ki fasal bahut achhi hui, aur usi saal logon ki income bhi badhi (aam normal good hai). Aam ke market ke baare mein kya PAKKA kaha ja sakta hai?
options: Equilibrium quantity badhegi; price badhegi ya giregi ye shifts ke size par depend karega
Price badhegi; quantity ka direction pata nahi
questions.explanation: Achhi fasal ⇒ supply right shift (P ↓, Q ↑). Income ↑ ⇒ demand right shift (P ↑, Q ↑). Dono quantity badhaate hain, to Q pakka badhegi. Price par dono ulta push karte hain, to price ka direction is par depend karega ki kaunsa shift bada hai. Options B aur C tabhi sahi hain jab ek shift ko dusre se bada maan lo, jo question mein diya nahi hai.

questions.question: Smartphones mein lagne wali chips sasti ho jaati hain. Smartphone market mein kya hoga?
options: Supply curve left shift hoga aur price badhegi
Demand curve right shift hoga aur price badhegi
Supply curve right shift hoga; price giregi aur quantity badhegi
Supply curve par movement hoga, supply same rahegi
questions.explanation: Chips ek **input** hain. Input sasta hone se har price par firms zyada bechna chahti hain, to supply curve right shift hota hai: equilibrium price girti hai aur quantity badhti hai. Left shift input mehenga hone par hota, input cost demand curve ko shift nahi karti, aur movement tab hota jab smartphone ki apni price badalti.

questions.question: Cricket bats aur cricket balls complements hain. Bats ki price bahut badh jaati hai. Cricket balls ke market mein kya hoga?
options: Balls ka demand curve left shift hoga
Balls ka demand curve right shift hoga
Balls ka supply curve right shift hoga
Balls ke demand curve par movement hoga
questions.explanation: **Complements** saath use hote hain. Bats mehenge hone se kam log cricket khelne ka saamaan khareedenge, to har price par balls ki demand kam hogi: demand curve left shift. Right shift substitutes ke case mein hota, bats ki price balls ki supply ko shift nahi karti, aur movement sirf balls ki apni price badalne par hota hai.

questions.question: Ek market mein price equilibrium price se upar hai. Kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Equilibrium se upar price par sellers zyada bechna chahte hain aur buyers kam khareedte hain, yaani Qs > Qd: **surplus**. Unsold stock clear karne ke liye sellers price ghataate hain, jab tak equilibrium na aa jaaye. Shortage tab hoti jab price equilibrium se neeche hoti, aur surplus mein price badhna law of supply and demand ke ulta hai.

questions.question: Ek market mein Qd = 150 − 3P aur Qs = 2P − 10 hai. Equilibrium price aur quantity kya hai?
questions.explanation: Qd = Qs: 150 − 3P = 2P − 10 ⇒ 160 = 5P ⇒ P* = ₹32. Q* = 150 − 3(32) = 54; check: 2(32) − 10 = 54 ✓. Q = 64 tab aata hai jab supply mein −10 bhool jaao (2 × 32), ₹28 tab jab 10 ko galat side le jaake 140 ÷ 5 karo, aur ₹40 par Qd = 30 aur Qs = 70 alag hain, to wo equilibrium nahi.

questions.question: Usi market mein (Qd = 150 − 3P, Qs = 2P − 10) agar price ₹40 par atak jaaye, to kya hoga?
questions.explanation: P = ₹40 par Qd = 150 − 120 = 30 aur Qs = 80 − 10 = 70. Qs > Qd, to 70 − 30 = **40 units ka surplus**. Price equilibrium (₹32) se upar hai, isliye shortage nahi ho sakti. 24 units equilibrium quantity 54 aur Qd 30 ka farq hai, aur 30 sirf quantity demanded hai, surplus nahi.

questions.question: Ek market mein Qd = 100 − 2P aur Qs = 3P − 20 hai. Logon ki income badhne se har price par demand 20 units badh jaati hai. Naya equilibrium price aur quantity kya hai?
questions.explanation: Naya demand: Qd = 120 − 2P. 120 − 2P = 3P − 20 ⇒ 140 = 5P ⇒ P = ₹28, Q = 120 − 56 = 64 (check: 84 − 20 = 64 ✓). Purana equilibrium P = ₹24, Q = 52 tha, to demand badhne se P aur Q dono badhe. Q = 72 maan leta hai ki price same rahegi aur poori 20 units extra bikengi, Q = 44 naye price ko purane demand mein daalne se aata hai, aur ₹32 tab aata hai jab 20 ko supply side par galat sign se jodo.

questions.question: Ek saal kharab mausam se soybean ki fasal kam hui (soybean oil ki supply ghati), aur usi saal ek sasta substitute oil market mein aaya (soybean oil ki demand ghati). Soybean oil market ke baare mein kya PAKKA kaha ja sakta hai?
options: Price ka direction pata nahi; quantity pakka giregi
Quantity ka direction pata nahi; price pakka badhegi
questions.explanation: Supply ghatne se P ↑ aur Q ↓. Demand ghatne se P ↓ aur Q ↓. Dono shifts Q ko neeche le jaate hain, isliye **quantity pakka giregi**; price par dono ke ulte asar hain, to direction shifts ke size par depend karta hai. 'Price badhegi' sirf supply shift dekhta hai, 'dono girenge' sirf demand shift, aur quantity ko uncertain kehna ulta hai.

questions.question: Ek chhote market mein do buyers hain: Ravi ki demand q = 20 − P aur Sita ki demand q = 30 − 2P (₹15 se upar Sita kuch nahi khareedti). Market supply Qs = 2P hai. Equilibrium price aur quantity kya hai?
questions.explanation: Market demand = individual demands ka **horizontal sum**: Q = (20 − P) + (30 − 2P) = 50 − 3P (₹15 tak). 50 − 3P = 2P ⇒ P = ₹10, Q = 20 (Ravi 10, Sita 10). ₹10 < ₹15, to Sita market mein hai ✓. ₹6.67 sirf Ravi ki demand use karta hai aur ₹7.5 sirf Sita ki, jabki ₹12.5 slopes jodte waqt −3P ki jagah −2P likhne se aata hai.

questions.question: Millet snacks ke market mein Qs = 4P − 40 hai aur demand Qd = a − 2P form ki hai. Pehle equilibrium price ₹20 tha. Ek popular food blogger ke review ke baad demand curve parallel shift hua aur naya equilibrium price ₹25 ho gaya. Har price par demand kitni units badhi?
questions.explanation: Pehle: Qs = 4(20) − 40 = 40, to 40 = a − 2(20) ⇒ a = 80. Baad mein: Qs = 4(25) − 40 = 60, to 60 = a′ − 2(25) ⇒ a′ = 110. Har price par demand 110 − 80 = **30 units** badhi. 20 units sirf equilibrium quantity ka badlaav (40 se 60) hai, jo shift se kam hai kyunki price badhne par buyers curve ke saath kuch quantity kam kar dete hain. 60 naya Q hai, aur 10 price ke badlaav (5) ko slope 2 se multiply karne par aata hai.

weeks.title: Elasticity: How Strongly Buyers and Sellers Respond
weeks.summary: Is week aap price, income aur cross-price elasticity nikaalna (midpoint method se), elastic aur inelastic demand ka farq, aur price change ka total revenue par asar samajhna seekhoge.
concepts: **Price elasticity of demand (Ed)** batati hai ki price badalne par quantity demanded kitni sensitive hai: Ed = % change in Qd ÷ % change in P. Law of demand ki wajah se ye negative hoti hai, isliye usually iski absolute value bolte hain.

**Midpoint method**: % change = (new − old) ÷ average of new and old × 100. Iska fayda: price badhe ya ghate, dono direction mein same elasticity aati hai. Simple % method mein base badalne se answer badal jaata hai.

**Elastic, inelastic, unit elastic**: |Ed| > 1 elastic (quantity zyada react karti hai), |Ed| < 1 inelastic, |Ed| = 1 unit elastic. Extreme cases: perfectly inelastic (vertical curve, Ed = 0) aur perfectly elastic (horizontal curve).

**Elasticity ke determinants**: close substitutes zyada ⇒ zyada elastic (ek brand ke biscuits); necessities kam elastic (namak, dawai); market narrowly define karo to zyada elastic; long run mein short run se zyada elastic; budget ka bada hissa ho to zyada elastic.

**Total revenue (TR = P × Q)**: demand elastic ho to price ↑ ⇒ TR ↓; inelastic ho to price ↑ ⇒ TR ↑; unit elastic ho to TR same. Isiliye bumper crop mein (inelastic demand) kisaanon ki total income gir sakti hai.

**Linear demand par elasticity badalti hai**: straight-line demand ka slope constant hai par elasticity nahi. Upar wale (high price) hisse mein elastic, neeche inelastic, aur bilkul beech mein unit elastic, jahan TR maximum hota hai.

**Income elasticity** = % change in Q ÷ % change in income. Positive ⇒ normal good (1 se zyada ⇒ luxury, 0 aur 1 ke beech ⇒ necessity); negative ⇒ inferior good. **Cross-price elasticity** = % change in Q of good X ÷ % change in price of good Y: positive ⇒ substitutes, negative ⇒ complements.
**Price elasticity of supply** = % change in Qs ÷ % change in P. Production jaldi badha sakte hon (spare capacity, long run) to supply zyada elastic hoti hai.

example.problem: Ek multiplex ne ticket price ₹200 se ₹250 kar di aur tickets 1,200 se ghat kar 900 per din ho gaye. Midpoint method se price elasticity nikaalo aur batao ki revenue badha ya ghata.
steps: |Ed| = 28.6 ÷ 22.2 ≈ 1.29, jo 1 se zyada hai, to demand elastic hai.
Elastic demand mein price badhaane se TR girta hai, aur numbers bhi yahi dikhaate hain.

mistakes: Simple % method use karna jab question midpoint maange. Base (old value) badalne se answer badal jaata hai; midpoint mein average se divide karo.
Slope aur elasticity ko same samajhna. Linear demand ka slope constant hai, par elasticity har point par alag hai.
Cross-price elasticity ka sign ulta padhna. Positive = substitutes, negative = complements; income elasticity mein negative = inferior good.
revision: |Ed| > 1 elastic, < 1 inelastic, = 1 unit elastic.
Midpoint % change = change ÷ average × 100.
Inelastic demand: price ↑ ⇒ TR ↑; elastic demand: price ↑ ⇒ TR ↓.
Linear demand ke midpoint par |Ed| = 1 aur TR maximum.
Income elasticity > 1 luxury, 0 se 1 necessity, < 0 inferior; cross elasticity > 0 substitutes, < 0 complements.

questions.question: Ek good ki demand **inelastic** hai. Seller price badhaata hai. Total revenue ka kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Inelastic demand mein quantity price ke percentage se kam girti hai. Price ka asar zyada hai, isliye P × Q badhta hai. 'TR girega' elastic demand ka case hai. Price badhne par quantity demanded kabhi nahi badhti (law of demand).

questions.question: Printers aur ink cartridges ke beech cross-price elasticity −0.8 hai. Ye dono goods kya hain?
questions.explanation: Negative cross-price elasticity ka matlab: cartridge mehenga hone par printers ki demand girti hai, yaani dono saath use hote hain: complements. Positive hoti to substitutes. Inferior good ka pata income elasticity se chalta hai, cross-price elasticity se nahi.

questions.question: Ek notebook ki price ₹40 se ₹60 hone par quantity demanded 120 se 80 ho jaati hai. Midpoint method se price elasticity (absolute value) kya hai?
questions.explanation: % change in Q = (80 − 120) ÷ 100 = −40%. % change in P = (60 − 40) ÷ 50 = 40%. |Ed| = 40 ÷ 40 = 1.0, unit elastic. Simple method se 120 aur 40 ko base lo to 33.3% ÷ 50% = 0.67 aata hai, aur ulti direction (80 aur 60 base) se 50% ÷ 33.3% = 1.5. Isiliye midpoint method use karte hain.

questions.question: Ek family ki monthly income ₹45,000 se ₹55,000 hone par uske restaurant meals 3 se 5 per month ho jaate hain. Midpoint method se income elasticity aur good ka type kya hai?
questions.explanation: % change in Q = 2 ÷ 4 = 50%. % change in income = 10,000 ÷ 50,000 = 20%. Income elasticity = 50 ÷ 20 = 2.5. Positive aur 1 se zyada ⇒ luxury, jo normal good ka type hai. 0.4 tab aata hai jab ratio ulta le lo (20 ÷ 50). Inferior good ke liye elasticity negative honi chahiye.

questions.question: Inme se kiski demand sabse zyada price elastic hone ki ummeed hai?
questions.explanation: Ek brand ke biscuits ke bahut saare close substitutes hain (doosre brands), to thodi si price badhne par log brand badal lete hain: highly elastic. Namak aur insulin necessities hain jinke substitutes kam hain. 'Food as a whole' broadly defined market hai; uska koi substitute nahi, isliye wo inelastic hai, bhale hi ek brand elastic ho.

questions.question: Ek seller ki demand Qd = 100 − 2P hai. Kis price par uska total revenue maximum hoga?
questions.explanation: TR = P × (100 − 2P). Kuch values: P = 20 ⇒ 20 × 60 = 1,200; P = 25 ⇒ 25 × 50 = 1,250; P = 30 ⇒ 30 × 40 = 1,200. Maximum P = 25 par hai, jo linear demand ka midpoint hai (choke price 50 ka aadha), jahan |Ed| = 1. ₹50 par Q = 0 aur TR = 0, wo trap hai. ₹20 aur ₹10 inelastic hisse mein hain, jahan price badhaane se TR badhta hai.

questions.question: Inme se kis good ki demand sabse zyada **inelastic** hone ki ummeed hai?
options: Ek particular brand ka cold drink
Ghar ki bijli (electricity), short run mein
questions.explanation: Bijli ek necessity hai, iske close substitutes kam hain, aur short run mein log appliances jaldi nahi badal sakte, isliye demand **inelastic** hai. Ek brand ka cold drink aur ek chain ka pizza narrowly defined markets hain jinke bahut substitutes hain, aur foreign holiday ek luxury hai jo budget ka bada hissa hota hai; ye teeno elastic hain.

questions.question: Ek good ki income elasticity −0.6 hai. Ye kis type ka good hai?
questions.explanation: Income elasticity negative hai, matlab income badhne par quantity girti hai: **inferior good**. Necessity aur luxury dono normal goods hain jinki income elasticity positive hoti hai (0 aur 1 ke beech, aur 1 se zyada). Complement cross-price elasticity ka concept hai, income elasticity ka nahi.

questions.question: Ek good ka demand curve bilkul **vertical** hai. Iski price elasticity of demand kya hai?
questions.explanation: Vertical demand curve ka matlab hai price kuch bhi ho, quantity same rehti hai: % change in Q = 0, to Ed = 0, yaani **perfectly inelastic**. Infinite elasticity horizontal curve ki hoti hai, unit elastic mein dono % changes barabar hote hain, aur elastic mein quantity price se zyada react karti hai.

questions.question: Coffee ki price ₹90 se ₹110 hone par chai ki quantity demanded 400 se 500 cups ho jaati hai. Midpoint method se cross-price elasticity kya hai, aur dono goods ka relation kya hai?
questions.explanation: % change in chai ki Q = (500 − 400) ÷ 450 ≈ 22.2%. % change in coffee ki P = (110 − 90) ÷ 100 = 20%. Cross elasticity = 22.2 ÷ 20 ≈ **1.11**, positive, to dono **substitutes** hain. 1.13 simple % method (400 aur 90 base: 25% ÷ 22.2%) se aata hai, 0.9 ratio ulta lene se, aur negative sign tab hota jab coffee mehngi hone par chai ki demand girti.

questions.question: Ek music app ki subscription ki price elasticity of demand 0.4 (absolute value) hai. Company price 10% badhaati hai. Total revenue ka lagbhag kya hoga?
questions.explanation: |Ed| = 0.4 ka matlab: price 10% badhe to quantity lagbhag 0.4 × 10 = 4% giregi. TR ka % change ≈ 10% − 4% = **lagbhag 6% badhega** (exactly 1.10 × 0.96 = 1.056). Demand inelastic hai, isliye price badhaane se revenue badhta hai. 4% girna sirf quantity ka asar hai, 14% quantity ke girne ko plus kar deta hai, aur 'same' sirf unit elastic demand mein hota.

questions.question: Ek seller ki demand Qd = 120 − 3P hai aur wo abhi ₹25 charge karta hai. Kya price thoda badhaane se uska total revenue badhega, aur TR kis price par maximum hai?
options: Haan, TR badhega; maximum TR ₹25 par
Nahi, TR girega; maximum TR ₹20 par
Haan, TR badhega; maximum TR ₹40 par
Nahi, TR girega; maximum TR ₹12.5 par
questions.explanation: Choke price (Qd = 0) = ₹40, to linear demand ka midpoint P = ₹20, Q = 60 hai, jahan demand unit elastic hai aur TR maximum hai (20 × 60 = ₹1,200). ₹25 midpoint se upar hai, yaani **elastic** hissa, isliye price badhaane se TR girega. Check: ₹25 par TR = 25 × 45 = ₹1,125 < ₹1,200. ₹40 par quantity zero hai (TR = 0), aur ₹12.5 current price ko aadha karne ki galti hai.

questions.question: Tomato ki price ₹20 se ₹30 per kg hone par kisaan supply 800 se 1,400 tonnes kar dete hain. Midpoint method se price elasticity of supply kya hai?
questions.explanation: % change in Qs = (1,400 − 800) ÷ 1,100 ≈ 54.5%. % change in P = (30 − 20) ÷ 25 = 40%. Es = 54.5 ÷ 40 ≈ **1.36**, to supply elastic hai. 1.5 simple % method (75% ÷ 50%) se aata hai, 1.88 dono methods mix karne se (75% ÷ 40%), aur 0.73 ratio ulta lene se.

questions.question: Gehu ki demand ki price elasticity 0.25 (absolute value) hai. Bumper crop ki wajah se bechne ke liye quantity 10% zyada hai. Market clear karne ke liye price lagbhag kitni girni chahiye, aur kisaanon ki total revenue ka kya hoga?
options: Price lagbhag 10% giregi; revenue same rahegi
questions.explanation: Ed = % change in Q ÷ % change in P ⇒ 0.25 = 10 ÷ %ΔP ⇒ price lagbhag **40% girni chahiye** taaki buyers 10% zyada lein. Demand inelastic hai, to price ka girna quantity ke badhne se kahin bada hai, aur TR girta hai (roughly 1.10 × 0.60 = 0.66, yaani lagbhag 34% kam). 2.5% elasticity ko multiply karne (0.25 × 10) se aata hai, 'revenue badhegi' elastic demand ka result hai, aur 10% unit elastic demand maan leta hai.

questions.question: Ek airline ke business-class tickets ki income elasticity 2.5 hai, aur premium train tickets ke saath cross-price elasticity 0.8 hai. Agar logon ki income 4% badhe aur premium train fares 5% ghatein, to business-class tickets ki demand lagbhag kitni badlegi?
questions.explanation: Income ka asar: 2.5 × 4% = +10%. Train fares girne ka asar: cross elasticity positive hai (substitutes), to 0.8 × (−5%) = −4%. Total ≈ 10% − 4% = **+6%**. +14% train ka asar plus kar deta hai (sign galat), +10% train fares ko ignore karta hai, aur −6% dono signs ulat deta hai.

weeks.title: Consumer Surplus, Producer Surplus and Market Efficiency
weeks.summary: Is week aap willingness to pay aur seller cost se consumer aur producer surplus nikaalna, graph par unke areas pehchaanna, aur ye samajhna seekhoge ki free market equilibrium total surplus ko maximum kyun karta hai.
concepts: **Willingness to pay (WTP)**: wo maximum amount jo ek buyer kisi good ke liye dene ko ready hai. Demand curve ki height har quantity par marginal buyer ki WTP dikhaati hai.

**Consumer surplus (CS)** = WTP − actually paid price. Market mein CS = demand curve ke neeche aur price line ke upar ka area. Linear demand ke liye ye ek triangle hai: ½ × Q* × (choke price − P*). Price girne par purane buyers ka CS badhta hai aur naye buyers bhi market mein aate hain.

**Seller cost aur producer surplus (PS)**: seller ki cost wo minimum price hai jis par wo bechne ko ready hai. PS = received price − cost. Market mein PS = price line ke neeche aur supply curve ke upar ka area.
**Total surplus** = CS + PS = buyers ki total value − sellers ki total cost. Ye batata hai ki market se society ko kitna net benefit mila.

**Efficiency**: allocation efficient tab hai jab total surplus maximum ho. Free market equilibrium par (1) goods unhi buyers ko jaate hain jinki WTP sabse zyada hai, (2) unhi sellers se aate hain jinki cost sabse kam hai, aur (3) quantity itni hoti hai ki aur ek unit ki value uski cost se kam ho. Equilibrium se kam ya zyada produce karna, dono total surplus ghataate hain.

**Equity vs efficiency**: efficiency ka matlab hai pie sabse bada hai; equity ka matlab hai pie fairly bata hai ya nahi. Market efficient ho sakta hai par unequal bhi. Policy mein dono ka trade-off sochna padta hai.

**Limits**: efficiency ka ye result tab hold karta hai jab market competitive ho aur koi externality na ho. Monopoly power ya pollution jaisi **market failures** mein market equilibrium efficient nahi hota (aage ke weeks mein).

example.problem: Ek local market mein (illustrative) Qd = 120 − 2P aur Qs = 3P − 30 hai. Equilibrium par consumer surplus, producer surplus aur total surplus nikaalo.

mistakes: Triangle ke area mein ½ bhool jaana. CS aur PS linear curves ke liye triangles hain, rectangles nahi.
CS ke liye triangle ki height galat lena. Height = choke price − market price, sirf choke price nahi.
Ye maan lena ki zyada output hamesha better hai. Equilibrium ke baad wali units ki cost unki value se zyada hai, isliye wo total surplus ghataati hain.
revision: CS = WTP − price; area = demand ke neeche, price ke upar.
PS = price − cost; area = price ke neeche, supply ke upar.
Total surplus = CS + PS = value − cost.
Competitive equilibrium total surplus maximise karta hai (no externalities).
Efficiency = pie ka size; equity = pie ka distribution.

questions.question: Ek used cricket bat ke 4 possible buyers hain, jinki WTP ₹500, ₹400, ₹300 aur ₹200 hai. Har buyer max ek bat lega aur market price ₹300 hai. Total consumer surplus kitna hai?
questions.explanation: ₹500 wala buyer ₹200 surplus paata hai, ₹400 wala ₹100, aur ₹300 wala ₹0 (indifferent). ₹200 wala buyer khareedega hi nahi. Total CS = 200 + 100 + 0 = ₹300. ₹200 tab aata hai jab ₹200 wale buyer ko bhi −₹100 ke saath gin lo, par koi negative surplus par nahi khareedta. ₹1,200 teen buyers ki total WTP hai, surplus nahi.

questions.question: Market graph par **producer surplus** kaunsa area hai?
options: Demand curve ke neeche aur price ke upar ka area
Demand aur supply curves ke beech ka area, equilibrium ke right side
Price line ke neeche aur supply curve ke upar ka area
questions.explanation: Supply curve har unit ke seller ki cost dikhata hai. PS = price − cost, isliye ye price line aur supply curve ke beech ka area hai (0 se Q* tak). Option A consumer surplus hai, aur P × Q total revenue hai, surplus nahi, kyunki usme se cost minus nahi hui.

questions.question: Ek good ki demand Qd = 80 − 2P hai aur market price ₹20 hai. Consumer surplus kitna hai?
questions.explanation: P = 20 par Q = 80 − 40 = 40. Choke price (Q = 0) = ₹40. CS = ½ × 40 × (40 − 20) = ₹400. ₹800 ½ bhoolne se aata hai, aur ₹1,600 tab jab height mein choke price hi le lo aur ½ bhi bhool jao.

questions.question: Usi demand (Qd = 80 − 2P) mein price ₹20 se girkar ₹15 ho jaati hai. Consumer surplus kitna badhta hai?
questions.explanation: Naya Q = 80 − 30 = 50, naya CS = ½ × 50 × (40 − 15) = ₹625. Purana CS ₹400 tha, to increase = ₹225. Isme do hisse hain: purane 40 buyers ko har ek par ₹5 bacha (₹200), aur 10 naye buyers ka triangle (½ × 10 × 5 = ₹25). Sirf ₹200 likhna naye buyers ko bhoolna hai, aur ₹625 naya total hai, change nahi.

questions.question: Ek competitive market (no externalities) mein agar kisi wajah se equilibrium se ZYADA quantity produce aur bechi jaaye, to total surplus ka kya hoga?
options: Total surplus badhega, kyunki zyada goods available hain
Consumer surplus badhega aur total surplus same rahega
Total surplus par koi farq nahi padega
Total surplus ghatega, kyunki extra units ki cost buyers ki value se zyada hai
questions.explanation: Q* ke baad supply curve demand curve ke upar hai: har extra unit banane ki cost us unit ki buyer ke liye value se zyada hai. Aisi har unit total surplus ko kam karti hai. 'Zyada goods hamesha better' wala option sabse tempting galti hai; efficiency value aur cost compare karke decide hoti hai, quantity se nahi.

questions.question: Ek market mein Qd = 100 − 2P aur Qs = 2P − 20 hai. Government sirf 20 units bechne ki permission deti hai (quota). Free market ke comparison mein kitna total surplus lose hota hai?
questions.explanation: Free market: 100 − 2P = 2P − 20 ⇒ P = 30, Q = 40. Choke price 50, supply start price 10, to TS = ½ × 40 × (50 − 10) = ₹800. Q = 20 par demand price = (100 − 20)/2 = 40 aur supply price = (20 + 20)/2 = 20. TS = curves ke beech ka area 0 se 20 tak = ½ × (40 + 20) × 20 = ₹600. Loss = 800 − 600 = ₹200 (ye triangle ½ × 20 × 20 hai). ₹600 bacha hua surplus hai, loss nahi.

questions.question: Meena ek book ke liye ₹600 tak dene ko ready thi, aur use wo book ₹450 mein mil gayi. Uska consumer surplus kitna hai?
questions.explanation: CS = WTP − paid price = ₹600 − ₹450 = **₹150**. ₹600 sirf uski WTP hai, ₹450 wo amount hai jo usne pay kiya, aur ₹1,050 dono ko jodne ki galti hai.

questions.question: Ek tailor ke liye ek shirt silne ka cost ₹300 hai, aur wo use ₹500 mein bechta hai. Is sale par uska producer surplus kitna hai?
questions.explanation: PS = received price − seller ka cost = ₹500 − ₹300 = **₹200**. ₹500 revenue hai, ₹300 cost hai, aur ₹800 dono ko jod deta hai; surplus hamesha dono ka farq hota hai.

questions.question: Ek market ka outcome total surplus ko maximum karta hai, par saara surplus kuch hi logon ko milta hai. Is outcome ke baare mein kya sahi hai?
options: Ye na efficient hai, na equitable
Ye efficient hai, par zaroori nahi ki equitable ho
Ye equitable hai, par efficient nahi
Total surplus maximum hai, to ye automatically fair bhi hai
questions.explanation: **Efficiency** ka matlab hai total surplus (pie) maximum hai, jo yahan sach hai. **Equity** ka sawaal hai ki pie fairly bata hai ya nahi, aur yahan surplus kuch logon tak simit hai. Isliye 'efficient nahi' wale options galat hain, aur 'maximum surplus = automatically fair' efficiency aur equity ko mix karta hai.

questions.question: Ek market mein supply Qs = 4P − 40 hai aur market price ₹30 hai. Producer surplus kitna hai?
questions.explanation: P = ₹30 par Qs = 120 − 40 = 80. Supply ka starting price (Qs = 0): 4P = 40 ⇒ P = ₹10. PS = ½ × 80 × (30 − 10) = **₹800**. ₹1,600 mein ½ bhool gaye, ₹1,200 height ko ₹30 le leta hai (₹10 minus nahi kiya), aur ₹2,400 sellers ka total revenue (P × Q) hai.

questions.question: 5 buyers ki WTP ₹90, ₹70, ₹60, ₹40 aur ₹20 hai, aur 5 sellers ke costs ₹10, ₹30, ₹50, ₹65 aur ₹80 hain. Har buyer max ek unit khareedta hai aur har seller max ek unit bechta hai. Total surplus maximum karne ke liye kitni units trade honi chahiye, aur maximum total surplus kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Sabse zyada WTP wale buyers ko sabse kam cost wale sellers se match karo: (90 − 10) + (70 − 30) + (60 − 50) = 80 + 40 + 10 = **₹130**. Chauthi unit mein value ₹40 cost ₹65 se kam hai, isliye wo surplus ₹25 ghataati hai (4 units par ₹105). 5 units par sirf ₹45 bachta hai, aur ₹220 sirf buyers ki value hai, sellers ka cost minus nahi kiya.

questions.question: Ek market mein Qd = 90 − 3P aur Qs = 2P − 10 hai. Equilibrium par consumer surplus aur producer surplus kitne hain?
questions.explanation: Equilibrium: 90 − 3P = 2P − 10 ⇒ P* = ₹20, Q* = 30. Demand ka choke price = 90 ÷ 3 = ₹30; supply ka starting price = 10 ÷ 2 = ₹5. CS = ½ × 30 × (30 − 20) = **₹150**, PS = ½ × 30 × (20 − 5) = **₹225**. Ulta pair CS aur PS ke areas swap karta hai, aur ₹300 ya ₹450 wale pairs mein triangle ka ½ bhool gaye.

questions.question: Ek market mein Qd = 120 − 2P aur Qs = 2P − 40 hai. Kisi wajah se 60 units produce aur consume hoti hain. Free-market equilibrium ke comparison mein total surplus kitna kam hai (deadweight loss)?
questions.explanation: Free market: 120 − 2P = 2P − 40 ⇒ P* = ₹40, Q* = 40. Q = 60 par buyers ki value (demand price) = (120 − 60) ÷ 2 = ₹30, par sellers ka cost (supply price) = (60 + 40) ÷ 2 = ₹50. Extra 20 units mein har unit ki cost uski value se zyada hai; loss triangle = ½ × 20 × (50 − 30) = **₹200**. ₹400 mein ½ bhool gaye, ₹100 height ko sirf ₹10 (ek side ka farq) leta hai, aur ₹0 ye maan leta hai ki zyada output se kabhi nuksaan nahi hota.

questions.question: Ek good ki demand Qd = 60 − P hai. Price ₹20 se badhkar ₹30 ho jaati hai. Consumer surplus kitna ghatega?
questions.explanation: P = ₹20 par Q = 40, CS = ½ × 40 × (60 − 20) = ₹800. P = ₹30 par Q = 30, CS = ½ × 30 × (60 − 30) = ₹450. Loss = 800 − 450 = **₹350**: rectangle 10 × 30 = ₹300 (jo buyers abhi bhi khareedte hain wo zyada dete hain) plus triangle ½ × 10 × 10 = ₹50 (jo buyers market chhod dete hain). ₹400 poori purani quantity par ₹10 ginta hai, ₹300 triangle bhool jaata hai, aur ₹450 naya CS hai, change nahi.

questions.question: Ek market mein 4 buyers (WTP ₹100, ₹80, ₹60, ₹40) aur 4 sellers (cost ₹20, ₹40, ₹70, ₹90) hain; har koi max ek unit leta ya deta hai. Ek lottery ke through 2 units ₹80 aur ₹40 WTP wale buyers ko jaati hain, aur ₹20 aur ₹40 cost wale sellers se aati hain. Efficient outcome ke comparison mein total surplus kitna kam hai?
questions.explanation: Efficient outcome mein units sabse zyada WTP wale buyers (₹100, ₹80) ko aur sabse kam cost wale sellers (₹20, ₹40) se jaati hain: TS = (100 + 80) − (20 + 40) = ₹120. Teesri unit (₹60 value, ₹70 cost) nahi bikni chahiye. Lottery mein sellers same hain par buyers ₹80 aur ₹40: TS = (80 + 40) − 60 = ₹60. Loss = **₹60**. Quantity same hai isliye '₹0 loss' maanna trap hai, kyunki efficiency ke liye goods sahi buyers tak bhi pahunchne chahiye. ₹120 efficient total surplus hai, loss nahi, aur ₹40 sirf lottery wale do buyers ki WTP ka farq (80 − 40) hai.

weeks.title: Price Controls, Taxes and Deadweight Loss
weeks.summary: Is week aap price ceiling aur price floor ka market par asar, tax ka burden buyers aur sellers mein kaise baṭta hai (tax incidence), aur tax se hone wala deadweight loss nikaalna seekhoge.
concepts: **Price ceiling**: legal maximum price. Agar ceiling equilibrium se upar hai to wo **non-binding** hai (koi asar nahi). Equilibrium se neeche ho to **binding**: Qd > Qs, yaani **shortage**. Phir rationing queues, black market ya 'jaan-pehchaan' se hoti hai. Rent control iska classic example hai.

**Price floor**: legal minimum price. Equilibrium se upar ho to binding aur **surplus** (Qs > Qd) banta hai; neeche ho to koi asar nahi. Minimum wage labour market mein floor hai. Jab government kisi crop ke liye minimum support price par khud surplus khareedti hai, to wo bhi floor jaisa kaam karta hai aur stocks jama hote hain.
**Tax ek wedge hai**: per-unit tax t lagne par buyers ka price (Pb) aur sellers ko milne wala price (Ps) alag ho jaate hain: Pb − Ps = t. Quantity equilibrium se kam ho jaati hai.

**Tax incidence**: tax kaanoon mein buyer par lage ya seller par, final outcome (Pb, Ps, Q) **same** rehta hai. Burden us side par zyada padta hai jo kam elastic (kam flexible) hai. Linear curves Qd = a − bP aur Qs = c + dP ke liye buyers ka share = d ÷ (b + d) × t.
**Tax revenue** = t × (tax ke baad wali quantity). Ye rectangle buyers aur sellers ke surplus se government ke paas jaata hai, isliye society ka loss nahi hai.

**Deadweight loss (DWL)**: wo surplus jo kisi ko nahi milta, kyunki kuch faydemand trades hote hi nahi. Linear curves ke liye DWL = ½ × t × (Q* − Q tax ke baad). Curves jitne zyada elastic, DWL utna zyada. Tax double karo to DWL lagbhag chaar guna ho jaata hai.

**Policy lesson**: price controls aur taxes ke peeche achhe intentions ho sakte hain, par wo prices ke signal ko bigaadte hain. Isliye policymakers ko shortage, surplus aur DWL jaise side effects bhi tolne padte hain.

example.problem: Ek market mein (illustrative) Qd = 120 − 2P aur Qs = 3P − 30 hai (equilibrium P* = ₹30, Q* = 60). Government sellers par ₹10 per unit tax lagaati hai. Buyer price, seller price, quantity, revenue aur DWL nikaalo.
steps: Sellers ko Ps = Pb − 10 milta hai, to supply Qs = 3(Pb − 10) − 30 = 3Pb − 60.
Burden: buyers ₹36 − ₹30 = ₹6 zyada dete hain, sellers ₹30 − ₹26 = ₹4 kam paate hain. Formula se bhi buyers ka share = 3/(2 + 3) × 10 = 6 ✓.

mistakes: Har ceiling ya floor ko binding maan lena. Pehle check karo: ceiling P* se neeche aur floor P* se upar ho tabhi asar hota hai.
Ye sochna ki jis par tax kaanoon mein lagta hai wahi poora pay karta hai. Burden elasticities se decide hota hai.
DWL mein tax revenue jod dena. Revenue government ke paas jaata hai; DWL sirf wo triangle hai jo kisi ko nahi milta.
revision: Binding ceiling (P < P*) ⇒ shortage; binding floor (P > P*) ⇒ surplus.
Tax wedge: Pb − Ps = t; Q ghatti hai.
Burden kam elastic side par zyada.
Revenue = t × Q_tax; DWL = ½ × t × ΔQ.
Tax buyer par lage ya seller par, result same.

questions.question: Government ek good par equilibrium price se NEECHE price ceiling lagaati hai. Kya hoga?
options: Shortage, kyunki quantity demanded quantity supplied se zyada hogi
Surplus, kyunki quantity supplied quantity demanded se zyada hogi
Price equilibrium tak badh jaayegi aur market clear ho jaayega
questions.explanation: Equilibrium se neeche ceiling binding hai: kam price par buyers zyada chahte hain aur sellers kam bechna chahte hain, to shortage banti hai. Price legally ceiling se upar nahi ja sakti, isliye option D galat hai. Surplus binding floor ka result hai.

questions.question: ₹5 per unit ka tax pehle sellers par lagaya jaata hai, phir policy badalkar wahi tax buyers par lagaya jaata hai. Burden ke baare mein kya sahi hai?
options: Buyers par lage to poora burden buyers uthaate hain
Sellers par lage to poora burden sellers uthaate hain
Dono cases mein burden ka division same hai; ye demand aur supply ki elasticities par depend karta hai
questions.explanation: Tax kis par legally lage, isse sirf ye badalta hai ki kaunsa curve shift hota hai. Final buyer price, seller price aur quantity same rehte hain. Burden ka split elasticities decide karti hain: kam elastic side zyada pay karti hai. 50-50 split sirf special case mein hota hai jab dono sides barabar responsive hon.

questions.question: Ek market mein Qd = 200 − 5P aur Qs = 3P − 40 hai. Government ₹25 ka price ceiling lagaati hai. Kya hoga?
options: Koi asar nahi, kyunki market price khud adjust ho jaayegi
questions.explanation: Equilibrium: 200 − 5P = 3P − 40 ⇒ 240 = 8P ⇒ P* = ₹30, Q* = 50. Ceiling ₹25 P* se neeche hai, to binding hai. P = 25 par Qd = 200 − 125 = 75 aur Qs = 75 − 40 = 35. Shortage = 75 − 35 = 40. 75 sirf quantity demanded hai, aur ceiling se neeche price par surplus nahi ban sakta.

questions.question: Ek market mein Qd = 90 − P aur Qs = 2P − 30 hai. Sellers par ₹6 per unit tax lagta hai. ₹6 mein se kitna burden buyers par padta hai?
questions.explanation: Bina tax: 90 − P = 2P − 30 ⇒ P* = ₹40, Q* = 50. Tax ke baad Qs = 2(Pb − 6) − 30 = 2Pb − 42. 90 − Pb = 2Pb − 42 ⇒ Pb = ₹44, Ps = ₹38. Buyers ₹4 zyada dete hain, sellers ₹2 kam paate hain. Supply zyada responsive hai (price ₹1 badalne par Qs 2 units badalta hai, Qd sirf 1), isliye buyers zyada burden uthaate hain. ₹2 sellers ka share hai, aur ₹6 tab jab maan lo poora tax buyers par gaya.

questions.question: Ek crop ka market equilibrium price ₹20 per kg hai. Government ₹15 per kg ka minimum price (price floor) announce karti hai. Kya hoga?
options: Koi asar nahi, kyunki floor binding nahi hai
questions.explanation: Price floor ka matlab hai price isse neeche nahi ja sakti. Market price ₹20 already ₹15 se upar hai, to floor kisi ko rokta hi nahi: non-binding, koi asar nahi. Surplus tab banta jab floor ₹20 se upar hota. Option D sabse bada trap hai: floor price ko neeche nahi kheenchta.

questions.question: Usi market mein (Qd = 90 − P, Qs = 2P − 30, sellers par ₹6 per unit tax) tax ka deadweight loss kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Bina tax Q* = 50, tax ke saath Pb = 44 par Q = 90 − 44 = 46. ΔQ = 4. DWL = ½ × 6 × 4 = ₹12. ₹24 ½ bhoolne se aata hai. ₹276 = 6 × 46 tax revenue hai, jo government ko milta hai, isliye wo deadweight loss nahi hai.

questions.question: Ek shehar ke labour market mein equilibrium wage ₹400 per din hai. Government ₹450 per din ka minimum wage set karti hai. Kya hoga?
options: Labour shortage, kyunki firms zyada workers chahengi
Koi asar nahi, kyunki floor binding nahi hai
Labour surplus (unemployment), kyunki kaam chahne wale workers firms ki demand se zyada honge
Wage girkar wapas ₹400 par aa jaayegi
questions.explanation: ₹450 equilibrium se **upar** hai, to floor binding hai: zyada log kaam karna chahte hain (labour supply ↑) aur firms kam workers rakhti hain (labour demand ↓), yaani surplus, jo unemployment ke roop mein dikhta hai. Floor equilibrium se neeche hota tabhi non-binding hota, shortage binding ceiling se banti hai, aur legal minimum ke neeche wage legally gir nahi sakti.

questions.question: Per-unit tax se government ko milne wale **tax revenue** ke baare mein kya sahi hai?
options: Ye society ka loss hai, isliye DWL mein jodte hain
Ye buyers aur sellers ke surplus se government ke paas jaata hai, society ka loss nahi hai
Ye hamesha sirf sellers ke surplus se aata hai
Ye tax × purani (bina tax wali) quantity hota hai
questions.explanation: Revenue = t × tax ke baad wali quantity. Ye surplus buyers aur sellers se government ke paas **transfer** hota hai aur public services mein use ho sakta hai, isliye society ka loss nahi. DWL sirf wo triangle hai jo kisi ko nahi milta. Revenue dono sides ke surplus se aata hai (kitna kisse, ye elasticities par depend karta hai), aur purani quantity use karna galat hai kyunki tax ke baad kam units bikti hain.

questions.question: Ek shehar mein auto fare ka market equilibrium ₹15 per km hai. Government ₹20 per km ka maximum fare (price ceiling) lagaati hai. Kya hoga?
options: Koi asar nahi, kyunki ceiling equilibrium se upar hai
Shortage hogi, kyunki ceiling lagi hai
Fare badhkar ₹20 per km ho jaayega
questions.explanation: Ceiling sirf maximum batati hai. Market fare ₹15 pehle se ₹20 se kam hai, to ceiling **non-binding** hai aur kuch nahi badalta. Shortage tab hoti jab ceiling equilibrium se neeche hoti, maximum fare ko target maan ke fare ₹20 tak badhna galat hai, aur surplus binding price floor se banta hai.

questions.question: Ek market mein Qd = 200 − 3P aur Qs = P − 20 hai. Buyers par ₹8 per unit tax lagaya jaata hai. Sellers ko milne wala price (Ps) kitna hoga?
questions.explanation: Bina tax: 200 − 3P = P − 20 ⇒ P* = ₹55. Buyers ka share = d ÷ (b + d) × t = 1 ÷ (3 + 1) × 8 = ₹2, to Pb = ₹57 aur Ps = 57 − 8 = **₹49**. Check: Qd = 200 − 171 = 29, Qs = 49 − 20 = 29 ✓. Demand zyada responsive hai, isliye sellers ₹6 ka bada burden uthaate hain, chahe tax buyers par laga ho. ₹57 buyers ka price hai, ₹47 maan leta hai ki poora tax sellers par gaya, aur ₹55 purana equilibrium hai.

questions.question: Usi market mein (Qd = 200 − 3P, Qs = P − 20, buyers par ₹8 per unit tax) government ko kitna tax revenue milega?
questions.explanation: Tax ke baad Q = 29 (Pb = ₹57, Ps = ₹49), to revenue = 8 × 29 = **₹232**. ₹280 purani quantity 35 use karta hai, ₹24 is tax ka DWL hai (½ × 8 × 6), aur ₹256 revenue aur DWL ko jod deta hai.

questions.question: Ek market mein Qd = 240 − 4P aur Qs = 4P − 80 hai. Government ₹30 ka price ceiling lagaati hai, aur sirf utni units bikti hain jitni supply hoti hai. Shortage kitni hai, aur agar ye units black market mein resell hon to buyers maximum kitni price dene ko ready honge?
questions.explanation: ₹30 par Qd = 240 − 120 = 120 aur Qs = 120 − 80 = 40, to shortage = 120 − 40 = **80 units**. Sirf 40 units available hain; demand curve par Q = 40 ke liye 40 = 240 − 4P ⇒ P = **₹50**, yaani black market price ₹50 tak ja sakti hai, equilibrium ₹40 se bhi zyada. ₹40 purana equilibrium hai, 40 units sirf bikne wali quantity hai shortage nahi, aur 120 sirf quantity demanded hai.

questions.question: Ek market mein Qd = 150 − 2P aur Qs = 3P − 50 hai. ₹5 per unit tax par deadweight loss kitna hai, aur tax ₹10 per unit karne par DWL kitna ho jaayega?
questions.explanation: Bina tax: 150 − 2P = 3P − 50 ⇒ P* = ₹40, Q* = 70. t = 5: buyers ka share = 3 ÷ 5 × 5 = 3, to Pb = ₹43, Q = 150 − 86 = 64, DWL = ½ × 5 × (70 − 64) = ₹15. t = 10: Pb = ₹46, Q = 58, DWL = ½ × 10 × 12 = ₹60. Tax double hua to quantity ka gap bhi double hua, isliye DWL **chaar guna** hua. DWL ko sirf double (₹30) maanna galat hai, aur ½ bhoolne se ₹30 aur ₹120 aate hain.

questions.question: Cigarettes ke market mein Qd = 100 − 0.5P aur Qs = 2P − 50 hai. Government sellers par ₹10 per pack tax lagaati hai. Buyers ka burden (Pb − purana P) aur tax ka DWL kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Bina tax: 100 − 0.5P = 2P − 50 ⇒ P* = ₹60, Q* = 70. Buyers ka share = d ÷ (b + d) × t = 2 ÷ 2.5 × 10 = ₹8, to Pb = ₹68, Ps = ₹58, Q = 100 − 34 = 66 (check: 116 − 50 = 66 ✓). DWL = ½ × 10 × (70 − 66) = ₹20. Kam elastic demand wale buyers zyaadatar burden uthaate hain chahe tax sellers par laga ho, isliye ₹2 (formula ulta) aur ₹5 (50-50 split) galat hain, aur ₹40 mein ½ bhool gaye.

questions.question: Ek crop ke market mein Qd = 500 − 10P aur Qs = 10P − 100 hai. Government ₹40 ka minimum support price set karti hai aur jo bhi surplus bachta hai wo khud usi price par khareedti hai. Government ko kitna kharch karna padega?
questions.explanation: ₹40 equilibrium (₹30) se upar hai, to floor binding hai. ₹40 par Qd = 500 − 400 = 100 aur Qs = 400 − 100 = 300, surplus = 200 units. Government ye 200 units ₹40 par khareedti hai: 200 × 40 = **₹8,000**. ₹6,000 purani price ₹30 use karta hai, ₹2,000 sirf price ka farq (₹10) ginta hai, aur ₹12,000 poori supply khareedna maan leta hai jabki 100 units buyers khud lete hain.

weeks.title: Externalities, Public Goods and Common Resources
weeks.summary: Is week aap seekhoge ki externalities mein market galat quantity kyun produce karta hai, Pigouvian tax aur Coase ka idea kaise madad karte hain, aur public goods aur common resources mein free rider aur overuse ki problem kya hai.
concepts: **Externality**: jab kisi ke action ka asar kisi teesre (bystander) par padta hai aur uska koi payment nahi hota. **Negative externality**: factory ka dhuaan, traffic congestion. **Positive externality**: vaccination, education, research. Market sirf private costs aur benefits dekhta hai, isliye externality ko ignore karta hai.

**Negative externality mein overproduction**: social cost = private cost + external cost. Market quantity wahan hoti hai jahan demand = private supply, par efficient (social optimum) quantity wahan hai jahan demand = social cost curve. Isliye market zyada produce karta hai aur DWL banta hai.

**Positive externality mein underproduction**: social value = private value + external benefit. Market efficient level se kam produce karta hai. Jaise vaccination: aapke vaccine se doosron ko bhi protection milti hai, par aap sirf apna fayda dekhte ho.

**Pigouvian tax aur subsidy**: per-unit tax jo external cost ke barabar ho, producers ko externality 'internalise' karwata hai aur market ko social optimum par le aata hai. Positive externality ke liye barabar size ki subsidy. Doosre tools: regulation (seedha limit lagana) aur **tradable pollution permits**, jisme pollution kam karna jinke liye sasta hai wahi zyada kam karte hain.

**Coase theorem**: agar private parties bina kharche ke (zero transaction costs) bargain kar sakti hain, to wo khud efficient solution tak pahunch jaayengi, chahe property right kisi ke bhi paas ho. Right kiska hai isse sirf ye badalta hai ki paisa kaun kisko deta hai. Real life mein zyada parties, legal costs ya mistrust ki wajah se bargaining aksar fail hoti hai.

**Goods ka classification**: **excludable** (kisi ko use karne se roka ja sakta hai?) aur **rival** (ek ke use se doosre ke liye kam bachta hai?). Private good: dono (samosa). Public good: dono nahi (street lights, national defence). Common resource: rival par non-excludable (samudra ki machhli, groundwater). Club good: excludable par non-rival (jab tak bheed na ho, jaise OTT subscription).

**Free rider problem**: public good ka fayda bina pay kiye bhi milta hai, to log contribute nahi karte aur market use kam ya bilkul provide nahi karta. Isliye government taxes se public goods provide karti hai, agar total benefit cost se zyada ho.

**Tragedy of the commons**: common resource ko har koi apne fayde ke liye zyada use karta hai kyunki cost sab mein baṭ jaati hai. Result: overfishing, groundwater ka girta level. Solutions: quotas, permits, user fees, ya property rights define karna.

example.problem: Ek chemical ke market mein (illustrative) demand P = 100 − Q aur private supply (private MC) P = 20 + Q hai. Har unit ₹20 ka pollution damage karti hai. Market quantity, efficient quantity, Pigouvian tax aur DWL nikaalo.
steps: Social MC = private MC + external cost = 40 + Q.
Social optimum: 100 − Q = 40 + Q ⇒ Q = 30, P = ₹70.
Market 10 units zyada produce kar raha hai. Q = 40 par social cost 80 hai par buyer value sirf 60.
Pigouvian tax = external cost = ₹20 per unit; isse private supply 40 + Q ban jaati hai aur market Q = 30 par aa jaata hai.
Answer: **market Q = 40, efficient Q = 30, tax ₹20 per unit, DWL ₹100**.

mistakes: Negative externality mein ye kehna ki market kam produce karta hai. Ulta hai: external cost ignore hone se market zyada produce karta hai.
Public good aur common resource mix karna. Dono non-excludable hain, par common resource rival hai (machhli khatam hoti hai), public good nahi.
Coase theorem ko 'right hamesha victim ko do' samajhna. Zero transaction costs mein outcome right ke allocation se independent hai; sirf payment ki direction badalti hai.
revision: Negative externality ⇒ overproduction ⇒ Pigouvian tax = external cost.
Positive externality ⇒ underproduction ⇒ subsidy.
Coase: zero transaction costs ⇒ efficient bargain, right kisi ke bhi paas ho.
Public: non-rival + non-excludable; common: rival + non-excludable.
Public goods mein free riding, common resources mein overuse.

questions.question: Ek colony ki street lights kis type ka good hain?
questions.explanation: Street light se kisi raahgir ko roka nahi ja sakta (non-excludable), aur ek ke roshni use karne se doosre ke liye kam nahi hoti (non-rival): public good. Common resource bhi non-excludable hai, par rival hota hai, jo yahan nahi hai.

questions.question: Open sea (kisi ki property nahi) ki machhliyaan kis category mein aati hain?
questions.explanation: Open sea mein kisi ko fishing se rokna mushkil hai (non-excludable), par jo machhli ek boat ne pakdi wo doosre ke liye nahi bachti (rival). Rival + non-excludable = common resource, jisme overfishing (tragedy of the commons) ka risk hota hai. Public good non-rival hota hai, isliye wo galat hai.

questions.question: Ek good ki demand P = 120 − 2Q aur private supply P = 30 + Q hai. Har unit se ₹15 ka external cost (pollution) hota hai. Market efficient quantity se kitni units zyada produce karta hai?
questions.explanation: Market: 120 − 2Q = 30 + Q ⇒ 3Q = 90 ⇒ Q = 30. Social cost = 45 + Q, to optimum: 120 − 2Q = 45 + Q ⇒ 3Q = 75 ⇒ Q = 25. Overproduction = 30 − 25 = 5 units. 30 aur 25 sirf market aur efficient quantities hain, farq nahi. 15 external cost (₹) hai, units nahi.

questions.question: Vaccination se sirf vaccine lene wale ko nahi, uske aas-paas ke logon ko bhi protection milti hai. Bina government ke market ke baare mein kya sahi hai?
options: Market efficient level se kam vaccination dega; subsidy se ise sudhaara ja sakta hai
Market efficient level se zyada vaccination dega; tax lagana chahiye
Market kam vaccination dega; isliye vaccine par tax lagana chahiye
questions.explanation: Ye positive externality hai: social benefit private benefit se zyada hai, par log sirf apna benefit dekh ke decide karte hain. Isliye market kam vaccination deta hai. Subsidy private benefit ko social benefit ke kareeb laati hai. Option D sahi diagnosis ke saath galat tool hai: tax quantity aur ghata deta.

questions.question: Ek factory ke pollution se paas ke farmer ko ₹50,000 per saal ka nuksaan hota hai. Factory ₹30,000 per saal mein filter laga ke pollution rok sakti hai. Transaction costs zero hain. Coase theorem ke hisaab se kya hoga?
options: Filter tabhi lagega jab clean water ka legal right farmer ke paas ho
Filter lagega, chahe right factory ke paas ho ya farmer ke paas
Filter kabhi nahi lagega, kyunki factory ko pollution ka cost nahi padta
Filter tabhi lagega jab government tax lagaaye
questions.explanation: Agar right farmer ka hai, to factory ke liye ₹30,000 ka filter ₹50,000 ka damage pay karne se sasta hai: filter lagega. Agar right factory ka hai, to farmer ₹30,000 se ₹50,000 ke beech kuch bhi dekar factory ko filter lagwaane ke liye manaa lega, kyunki uska nuksaan ₹50,000 hai. Dono cases mein efficient outcome (filter) aata hai; sirf ye badalta hai ki kaun pay karta hai. Option A sabse tempting trap hai.

questions.question: Ek housing society ke 100 residents mein se har ek ke liye common CCTV system ki value ₹500 hai. System ka cost ₹30,000 hai, aur CCTV ka fayda sab residents ko milega, chahe unhone pay kiya ho ya nahi. Kya sahi hai?
options: System nahi lagna chahiye, kyunki har resident ki value ₹500 cost ₹30,000 se bahut kam hai
System lagna chahiye, aur voluntary contributions se paisa aasaani se jama ho jaayega
System nahi lagna chahiye, kyunki CCTV ek private good hai
System lagna chahiye (₹50,000 > ₹30,000), par voluntary funding free riding ki wajah se fail ho sakti hai
questions.explanation: Public good ke liye total benefit = sabki values ka sum = 100 × ₹500 = ₹50,000, jo cost ₹30,000 se zyada hai, to system efficient hai. Par fayda bina pay kiye bhi milega, isliye har resident sochega 'baaki pay kar denge': free rider problem. Isiliye society ek compulsory maintenance charge lagaati hai, jaise government tax lagaati hai. Option A ek insaan ki value ko poori cost se compare karne ki galti hai.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa **positive externality** ka example hai?
options: Padosi ka raat mein loud music bajaana
Ek factory ka nadi mein waste daalna
Ek resident ka ghar ke bahar garden lagaana jise sab raahgir enjoy karte hain
Ek customer ka mehnga phone khareedna
questions.explanation: Garden ka fayda raahgiron (bystanders) ko bhi milta hai aur wo iske liye pay nahi karte: **positive externality**. Loud music aur nadi mein waste doosron par bina payment ke cost daalte hain, yaani negative externalities. Phone khareedna ek normal market transaction hai jisme koi third party affected nahi.

questions.question: Ek toll wala highway jahan traffic bahut kam hai (bheed kabhi nahi hoti), kis type ka good hai?
questions.explanation: Toll se bina pay kiye logon ko roka ja sakta hai (**excludable**), aur khaali road par ek gaadi ke chalne se doosron ke liye jagah kam nahi hoti (**non-rival**): ye club good hai. Public good non-excludable hota, common resource rival hota, aur private good excludable aur rival dono hota hai.

questions.question: Ek gaon ke common grazing ground par har family zyada se zyada gaayein charaati hai, aur dheere-dheere ghaas khatam ho jaati hai. Ise kya kehte hain?
options: Public good ka free rider problem
questions.explanation: Grazing ground **rival** hai (ek ki gaay ne jo ghaas khaayi wo doosre ke liye nahi bachi) par **non-excludable** hai (kisi ko roka nahi jaata). Har family ko poora fayda milta hai par nuksaan sab mein baṭ jaata hai, isliye overuse hota hai: **tragedy of the commons**. Free rider problem public goods ke underprovision ki baat hai, Coase theorem bargaining ki, aur yahan externality negative hai, positive nahi.

questions.question: Ek good ki demand P = 90 − Q aur private supply (private MC) P = 10 + Q hai. Har unit se ₹16 ka external cost (pollution) hota hai. Social optimum quantity aur sahi Pigouvian tax kya hai?
questions.explanation: Social MC = 10 + Q + 16 = 26 + Q. Social optimum: 90 − Q = 26 + Q ⇒ Q = 32. Pigouvian tax = per-unit external cost = **₹16**, jisse private supply social MC ke barabar ho jaati hai. Q = 40 market quantity hai (externality ignore), ₹8 tax ko aadha karne ki galti hai, aur 24 market Q se seedha 16 minus karne se aata hai, jabki quantity sirf 8 kam hoti hai.

questions.question: Do factories A aur B mein se har ek apna pollution 10 tons tak kam kar sakti hai. 1 ton kam karne ka cost A ke liye ₹2,000 aur B ke liye ₹8,000 hai. Government total 10 tons kam karwana chahti hai aur tradable pollution permits use karti hai. Efficient outcome kya hoga?
options: Dono 5-5 tons kam karenge; total cost ₹50,000
B saare 10 tons kam karegi; total cost ₹80,000
A 8 tons aur B 2 tons kam karegi; total cost ₹32,000
A saare 10 tons kam karegi; total cost ₹20,000
questions.explanation: Permits ka market pollution kam karne ka kaam usko deta hai jiske liye wo sabse sasta hai. A ke liye har ton ₹2,000 aur B ke liye ₹8,000 hai, to B, A se permits khareedegi aur **A saare 10 tons** kam karegi: 10 × 2,000 = ₹20,000. 5-5 ka split (₹50,000) ek seedhi regulation jaisa hai jo mehenga padta hai, B se saara kaam karwana sabse mehenga hai, aur 8-2 split bhi B ke mehenge tons rakh leta hai (₹32,000).

questions.question: Ek chemical ki demand P = 150 − 2Q aur private MC P = 30 + Q hai. Har unit ₹24 ka pollution damage karti hai. Bina government intervention ke market ka deadweight loss kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Market: 150 − 2Q = 30 + Q ⇒ Q = 40. Social MC = 54 + Q, to optimum: 150 − 2Q = 54 + Q ⇒ Q = 32. Market 8 units zyada banata hai, aur Q = 40 par social cost aur buyer value ka gap ₹24 hai (94 vs 70): DWL = ½ × 8 × 24 = **₹96**. ₹192 mein ½ bhool gaye, ₹960 poore external damage (24 × 40) ko DWL maan leta hai, aur ₹48 triangle ki height aadhi le leta hai.

questions.question: Skill-training courses ki private demand P = 100 − Q hai aur MC ₹40 constant hai. Har course se society ko ₹20 ka external benefit milta hai (zyada productive workforce). Market efficient level se kitne courses kam deta hai, aur kitni per-unit subsidy efficient level la degi?
questions.explanation: Market: private value = MC ⇒ 100 − Q = 40 ⇒ Q = 60. Social value = 120 − Q, to optimum: 120 − Q = 40 ⇒ Q = 80. Market **20 courses kam** deta hai. Subsidy = external benefit = ₹20 per unit; isse buyers ka effective price ₹20 ho jaata hai aur 100 − Q = 20 ⇒ Q = 80. ₹40 MC ko subsidy maan leta hai, 60 market quantity hai gap nahi, aur positive externality par tax quantity ko aur ghata dega.

questions.question: Ek restaurant ke generator ki awaaz se padosi ke home-studio ko ₹60,000 per saal ka nuksaan hota hai. Restaurant ₹40,000 per saal mein silencer laga sakta hai. Transaction costs zero hain aur shor karne ka legal right restaurant ke paas hai. Coase theorem ke hisaab se kya hoga?
options: Silencer nahi lagega, kyunki right restaurant ke paas hai
Padosi restaurant ko ₹40,000 se ₹60,000 ke beech pay karega aur silencer lagega
Restaurant padosi ko ₹60,000 compensation dega aur generator chalta rahega
Restaurant apne kharche par silencer lagaayega
questions.explanation: Silencer ka cost (₹40,000) nuksaan (₹60,000) se kam hai, to efficient outcome hai **silencer lagna**. Right restaurant ke paas hai, to padosi use pay karega: ₹40,000 se kam par restaurant nahi maanega aur ₹60,000 se zyada padosi nahi dega, to deal beech mein hogi. 'Right ki wajah se nahi lagega' Coase theorem ko ignore karta hai. Restaurant ka apne kharche par lagaana tab hota jab right padosi ke paas hota, aur ₹60,000 compensation silencer (₹40,000) se mehenga hai, to koi rational restaurant wo nahi chunega.

questions.question: Ek gaon mein naye footbridge ki value 50 families ke liye ₹2,000 each, 30 families ke liye ₹1,000 each aur 20 families ke liye ₹500 each hai. Bridge ka cost ₹1,20,000 hai aur bridge sab use kar sakte hain. Kya sahi hai?
options: Nahi banna chahiye, kyunki koi family akele ₹1,20,000 nahi degi
Nahi banna chahiye, kyunki average value sirf ₹1,400 hai
Banna chahiye, kyunki 50 families ki value hi ₹1,00,000 hai
Banna chahiye, kyunki kul value ₹1,40,000 cost se zyada hai
questions.explanation: Bridge public good hai (non-rival, non-excludable), to sabki values **jodte** hain: 50 × 2,000 + 30 × 1,000 + 20 × 500 = 1,00,000 + 30,000 + 10,000 = ₹1,40,000 > ₹1,20,000, to banna chahiye (free riding ki wajah se ise taxes se fund karna padega). Ek family ki value ya average value (₹1,400) ko poore cost se compare karna galat hai. Sirf ₹1,00,000 dekh ke conclusion lena bhi galat reasoning hai, kyunki wo akela cost se kam hai.

weeks.title: Comparative Advantage, Gains from Trade and Tariffs
weeks.summary: Is week aap absolute aur comparative advantage ka farq, specialisation se trade ke gains, world price par kaun gain aur kaun lose karta hai, aur tariff ya quota ka asar (revenue aur deadweight loss) nikaalna seekhoge.
concepts: **Absolute advantage**: jo producer kisi good ko kam inputs (jaise kam ghante) mein bana sakta hai. **Comparative advantage**: jo producer kisi good ko kam **opportunity cost** par bana sakta hai. Trade ka pattern comparative advantage decide karta hai, absolute nahi.

**Opportunity cost nikaalna**: agar output per worker diya ho, to 1 unit X ki cost = Y ka output ÷ X ka output. Agar hours per unit diye hon, to 1 unit X ki cost = X ke hours ÷ Y ke hours. Ek desh dono goods mein comparative advantage nahi rakh sakta, kyunki ek ki cost doosre ki cost ka ulta (reciprocal) hai.

**Specialisation aur gains from trade**: har desh us good mein specialise kare jisme uski opportunity cost kam hai, phir trade kare. Total output badhta hai aur dono apne PPF ke bahar consume kar sakte hain. Ye tab bhi sach hai jab ek desh dono goods mein absolute advantage rakhta ho.

**Terms of trade**: dono ko fayda tabhi hoga jab trade ki price dono deshon ki opportunity costs ke beech ho. Agar India ke liye 1 m cloth = 2 kg rice aur doosre desh ke liye 3 kg rice, to price 2 aur 3 kg rice ke beech honi chahiye.

**World price aur trade**: agar world price domestic price se upar hai to desh **exporter** banta hai: producers gain, consumers lose, total surplus badhta hai. Neeche hai to **importer** banta hai: consumers gain, producers lose, phir bhi total surplus badhta hai. Gainers losers ko compensate kar sakte hain.

**Tariff**: imports par tax. Domestic price world price + tariff ho jaati hai: domestic production badhta hai, consumption girta hai, imports ghatte hain. Government ko revenue = tariff × naye imports. Do DWL triangles bante hain: zyada mehenga domestic production aur kam consumption.

**Import quota**: imports ki seedhi limit. Effect tariff jaisa hi hai (domestic price badhti hai), par jo revenue jaisa gap hai wo licence holders ke paas jaata hai jab tak government licences auction na kare.

**Trade restriction ke arguments**: jobs bachana, national security, infant industry (nayi industry ko time dena), unfair competition, bargaining chip. Economists maante hain ki inme se zyaadatar cases mein restriction ka total cost uske benefit se zyada hota hai, isliye targeted support behtar hai.

example.problem: Ek worker ek din mein India mein 6 kg rice ya 3 m cloth bana sakta hai, aur Country Z mein 12 kg rice ya 4 m cloth (illustrative). Kaun kya export kare, aur kis price par dono ko fayda hoga?
steps: Absolute advantage: Z dono goods mein aage hai (12 > 6 aur 4 > 3).
India mein 1 m cloth ki opportunity cost = 6 ÷ 3 = 2 kg rice. Z mein = 12 ÷ 4 = 3 kg rice.
Cloth India mein sasta hai (2 < 3), to India ka comparative advantage cloth mein hai.
Rice ki cost: India mein 1 kg = 0.5 m cloth, Z mein = 0.33 m cloth, to Z ka comparative advantage rice mein hai.
Terms of trade 2 aur 3 kg rice per m cloth ke beech honi chahiye, jaise 2.5 kg.
India ka worker 3 m cloth banaakar 7.5 kg rice le sakta hai, jabki khud sirf 6 kg banata. Z ko 1 m cloth 2.5 kg rice mein milta hai, khud banaane mein 3 kg lagte.
Answer: **India cloth export kare, Z rice export kare; 2 aur 3 kg rice per m cloth ke beech koi bhi price (jaise 2.5) dono ko gain deti hai**.

mistakes: Absolute advantage dekh ke trade pattern decide karna. Fix: hamesha opportunity cost compare karo.
Hours per unit wale table mein output per hour wala formula lagana. Hours diye hon to cost = apne hours ÷ doosre good ke hours.
Tariff ke DWL mein tariff revenue jod dena. Revenue government ko jaata hai; DWL sirf do triangles hain.
revision: Comparative advantage = kam opportunity cost.
Ek desh dono goods mein comparative advantage nahi rakh sakta.
Terms of trade dono opportunity costs ke beech.
Importer: consumers gain > producers lose; exporter: producers gain > consumers lose.
Tariff ⇒ price ↑, imports ↓, revenue = t × imports, do DWL triangles.

questions.question: Kisi desh ka kisi good mein **comparative advantage** hone ka matlab kya hai?
options: Wo good kam inputs mein bana sakta hai
Wo good sabse zyada quantity mein bana sakta hai
Wo good kam opportunity cost par bana sakta hai
Wo good already export karta hai
questions.explanation: Comparative advantage opportunity cost ka comparison hai: doosre goods ka kitna chhodna padta hai. Kam inputs mein banana absolute advantage hai, jo trade ka pattern decide nahi karta. Ek desh har good mein absolute advantage rakh sakta hai, par comparative advantage sirf kuch goods mein.

questions.question: Ek desh mein steel ki domestic price world price se zyada hai. Free trade shuru hone par us desh mein kya hoga?
options: Desh import karega: consumers gain, domestic producers lose, aur total surplus badhega
Desh export karega: producers gain, consumers lose
Consumers aur producers dono lose karenge
Consumers gain, producers lose, aur total surplus ghatega
